newsitem.title: USA: Dole flies long distance for a cup of coffee.
newsitem.headline: Dole flies long distance for a cup of coffee.

text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole flew from Detroit to New Jersey before dawn on Saturday for a cup of coffee and cheers at a diner on his 96-hour, non-stop run to the election.
Dole, 73, and his flying caravan of reporters and staff arrived at the old-fashioned Bendix Diner here near Hackensack to a cheering reception by about 300 supporters.
Nothing unusual about a campaign crowd, except this group showed up well before Dole to see him arrive at 4:44 a.m. EST at the diner after a 414-mile plane ride and short bus trip.
Accompanied by New Jersey Republican Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, Dole had a cup of coffee and chatted with owner Anthony Diakakis, a Democrat, who said he was supporting Dole.

Urged by the sign-waving crowd outside to "speak, speak, speak," Dole said through a hand-held microphone: "If there's this much enthusiasm in New Jersey and New York and this area, we're gonna win just like the Yankees won."
The crowd, obviously Yankee baseball fans, roared approval at the mention by Dole of the World Series champions who came from behind to win against the Atlanta Braves.

Over a 24-hour period, Dole said he had slept for about an hour on the plane between Detroit and New Jersey. He has pledged to campaign solidly for 96 hours until Election Day, taking only catnaps and breaking for showers.
